title: The document-model README still installs @acaldas/document-model-libs and points at a personal docs site, so its package name and links predate the Powerhouse namespace
content:
`packages/document-model/README.md` opens with:

```
npm install @acaldas/document-model-libs
```

and documents interaction with a document through imports like `@acaldas/document-model-libs/budget-statement`, pointing at `acaldas.github.io/document-model-libs` for full documentation.

That is the package's pre-Powerhouse identity. The directory now publishes **`document-model`**, which is what every current import in the monorepo and in generated projects uses — including the `document-model/mock` subpath that the Academy's test tutorials were corrected to at this tag.

What is still useful in the file is the *shape* it teaches: a document can be driven **functionally** (`actions`, `reducer`, `utils` — `utils.createDocument(...)` then `reducer(doc, actions.addAccount(...))`) as well as through a class-style controller. That functional triple is exactly what generated document models still export.

The reading rule: take the API shape, ignore every package name and URL in it. A newcomer following its install line gets an unrelated, unmaintained package.
